card.summary: 1 GB free. Free accounts can upload 10 GB per file but only hold 1 GB total. Paid: S3-compatible 'FileLu S5', 1 PB scale. Lifetime promo: 1 TB $149, 2 TB $24...

free_tier.stated: 1 GB free. Free accounts can upload 10 GB per file but only hold 1 GB total. Paid: S3-compatible 'FileLu S5', 1 PB scale. Lifetime promo: 1 TB $149, 2 TB $249, 4 TB $449, 8 TB $649. 1 TB monthly transfer per 1 TB of purchased storage.

egress.terms: No request or retrieval fees. '$0 request or retrieval fees' is stated on the homepage and repeated as 'No request fees' / 'Always free' for S5. Transfer quota is tied 1:1 to storage purchased (buy 1 TB, get 1 TB/month).

record.tooling: Very wide: S3 (S5), WebDAV, FTP/FTPS, Rsync, rclone, REST API. rclone has a native Tier-1 backend (read-only in the table, ModTime R). Explicitly named as compatible with AWS CLI, rclone, Restic, Kopia, Proxmox, Duplicacy, Duplicati, S3 Browser, FileBrowserGO, Synology Hyper Backup, s3cmd, Cyberduck, Mountain Duck.
record.chaining: Purchased 8 TB lifetime plan at $649 supports Rsync and S3, serving as a backup target for tools like Duplicati, Kopia, and restic. Transfer is bound by a 1:1 transfer to storage capacity ratio.
record.limits_note: per-object: 10 GB/file on free, no limit on premium. Transfer is 1:1 with storage purchased, which is the binding constraint at archive-restore time.
record.reliability_note: 146,000 users; lifetime promos move between $149 and $350 list, so the lifetime price is a channel promotion rather than a stable list price. Read-only rclone classification means rclone cannot write; S3/Rsync/WebDAV must carry writes.
